text.p: Zinc, germanium, coal and emerging copper/gold miner, Savage Resources Ltd is currently undervalued and is attractive on asset based and cashflow valuation methods, brokerage Macquarie Equities Ltd said.

In its September equities round-up report, Macquarie recommended investors buy Savage stock based on the strong cash generation potential of the company's mining operations and its exposure to the strong germanium metal market.
Savage owns 49 percent of the Ernest Henry copper/gold project in northern Queensland which is scheduled to start production in late 1997.

"The net present value of the Ernest Henry mine combined with the other assets suggest the stock is undervalued at present and therefore is recommended as a core portfolio holding," the Macquarie report said.
The remaining 51 percent stake in Ernest Henry is owned by MIM Holdings Ltd.

Macquarie said the by-product metal germanium production from Savage's three U.S. zinc mines in Tennessee improved substantially in the last year and Savage now produces 20 percent of the world's supply.
The report said the outlook for the price of germanium was very strong due to the use of the metal in new products such as infra-red lenses, fibre optics and recyclable plastics.
"(Germanium) prices just 18 months ago were around US$250 per tonne. There are some spot deliveries being made now at well over US$1,000 per tonne," the report said.
Macquarie said Savage had been successful at locking in a large percentage of its 1997 production at high prices.
At 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), Savage shares were steady at A$1.27. At the time Macquarie published the report, Savage shares were trading at A$1.22. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
